title: What my opinion is on what is an acceptable way to use AI for game dev
author: PerfectEast6006
selftext:
Here is what I personally think is acceptable to use AI for. I am also much more lenient than most because AI carries a lot of stigma.

\- DO's

AI Programming: DO

Only technical tasks. Nobody cares because it has no artistic integrity, but be aware that AI will not do anything that you don't specifically prompt it to do. You might not even know the terminology needed to prompt it properly ("Inverse Kinematics", "raycast"). Understand everything that AI generates, even if you learn it later. You still need to learn it all; otherwise, you won't be able to expand or maintain code that you don't understand.

AI UI/UX design: DO

It leans more towards the technical side and works only if it doesn't have that AI look. Avoid generating logos or text; even using a basic font is better.

\- DON'Ts

AI Art assets 3D Models/Music/Art: DON'T.

Art is a conversation between the creator and the person who consumes it. It's irreplaceable. Many games have used bad art styles to an advantage, and I would prefer it if you just added free ambient sound effects rather than AI music.

Exception: I believe it is acceptable if the AI art itself is meant to be meaningless or inconsequential, such as a simple flame/VFX animation, or any basic static objects.

Writing: DON'T.

People hate AI writing, no matter what. If I wanted to talk to a chatbot or have a chatbot tell me a story, I would do that instead. (Strictly correcting grammar is OK. AI translated localizations would be OK to make it more accessible)

Game design: DON'T.

Being able to do game design requires a lot of effort, just as coding does. Coding is only half the story; your gameplay needs to be balanced, and that is much more difficult (AI simply can't just predict how a human would actually react to your gameplay). Interact with your playtesters and get a lot of feedback.

AI Voice: DON'T

AI voices are incapable of showing nuanced emotion. At least it's better than the TTS voices used in older YouTube videos, but I would rather hear your own voice or just have text. Otherwise, it feels just as unprofessional as TTS.

Cyber security (running a game server): DONT  
  
AI doing cyber security is as reckless as  the idea of AI trying to perform a surgery.

comments.author: TashLai
comments.body:
So basically "if you're an artist with zero progamming skills it's a free game, not the other way around".

Than you and no thank you. I'll keep my very human artistic judgement but make AI do the technical (should i say mechanical?) part of creating assets.

replies.author: Dauntle55Duck
replies.body:
Have you actually ever *tried* to make art? Picasso is super famous and his stuff looks weird, you don’t need to some magical skills to make something that people will resonate with!

I know, ai is easy and quick, but i don’t think it’s wrong to not want to miss out on the weirdness that makes art so human. I mean people spend *years* analyzing why some guy painted stripes, why should video games be exempt of the same search for intent and beauty

replies.author: TashLai
replies.body:
Idk how that counters anything i said. Modern engines let you create games with sub junior level progamming skills.

And you can very well spend years analyzing 800 000 dwarf fortress' code. You can begin now. Code shouldn't be exempt of the same search for *intent* and intelligence (and yes there's beauty in it too, it's just not as shiny).

I'm really tired of people dismissing programming as some unimportant mechanical skill. I'm gonna vibe making all the art just to piss y'all off.

replies.author: Dauntle55Duck
replies.body:
I don’t disagree tbh, it’s also a form of art in a way. I much prefer finding code from people online and building it up from fragments I learned from different people.

It’s the same way I learned to draw, find pieces and styling I love from others and build up from there.

I really I hate the divide between “artist” and “programmer” neither is too hard when you actually go and try but it will be if you view the other as different from who you are. 

I thought coding wasn’t really in my wheel house a few years back, but I had to use it and I fell in love with it. It makes me a bit sad that many people may not get that experience now

replies.author: TashLai
replies.body: There's no divide. The divide is created by people who say it's ok to use AI for coding but not art. I admire good artists as much as i admire good coders. I'm just being a little sarcastic here.
